Calcaneal spur.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcaneal spur.question: The _____ was Medical condition of the heel.
Calcaneal spur.fact: A calcaneal spur (also called a heel spur) is a bony outgrowth from the calcaneal tuberosity (heel bone). Calcaneal spurs are typically detected by x-ray examination.

Calcaneus.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcaneus.question: The _____ was Bone of the tarsus of the foot.
Calcaneus.fact: The calcaneus (; from the Latin calcaneus or calcaneum, meaning heel; pl.: calcanei or calcanea) or heel bone is a bone of the tarsus of the foot which constitutes the heel.

Calcar.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcar.question: The _____ was Spur of cartilage in bats.
Calcar.fact: The calcar, also called the calcaneum, is the name given to a spur of cartilage arising from inner side of ankle and running along part of outer interfemoral membrane in bats, as well as to a similar spur on the legs of some arthropods. The calcar serves to help spread the interfemoral membrane, which is part of the wing membrane between the tail and the hind legs.

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcareous nannofossils.question: The _____ was Class of microscopic fossils.
Calcareous nannofossils.fact: Calcareous nannofossils are a class of tiny (less than 30 microns in diameter) microfossils that are similar to coccoliths deposited by the modern-day coccolithophores. The practical applications of calcareous nannofossils in the areas of biostratigraphy and paleoecology became clear once deepwater drilling took off in 1968 with the Deep Sea Drilling Project, and they have been extensively studied ever since.

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcareous nannofossils.question: Research of the nannoplankton systematics in the early 20th century (Erwin Kamptner, Georges Deflandre, and Trygve Braarud) enabled M. N. Bramlette and W. R. Riedel to successfully use the nannofossil

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calcareous nannofossils.fact: The Deep Sea Drilling Project (DSDP, 1968) revealed the power of the technique: stratigraphic positions were found within minutes after the drilling core was hauled aboard the ship.

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcareous nannofossils.question: The term "calcareous nannofossil" was chosen in the _____ publications (although it was rarely used prior to that) and gained popularity afterwards, in the early 1970s

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcareous nannofossils.question: "Calcareous" is derived from _____: calx, "lime", and means "containing lime"

Calcareous nannofossils.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcareous nannofossils.question: The calcareous nannoplankton biodiversity grew in the _____ and Cretaceous periods peaking at about 150 species in the Late Cretaceous

Calcific tendinitis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calcification.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcification.question: The _____ was Accumulation of calcium salts in bodily tissue, usually bone.
Calcification.fact: Calcification is the accumulation of calcium salts in a body tissue. Calcifications may be classified on whether there is mineral balance or not, and the location of the calcification.

Calcinosis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcinosis.question: The _____ was Formation of calcium deposits in soft tissue.
Calcinosis.fact: Calcinosis is the formation of calcium deposits in any soft tissue.

Calcinosis cutis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcinosis cutis.question: The _____ was Medical condition in which calcium deposits form in the skin.
Calcinosis cutis.fact: Calcinosis cutis is an uncommon condition marked by calcium buildup in the skin and subcutaneous tissues. Calcinosis cutis can range in intensity from little nodules in one area of the body to huge, crippling lesions affecting a vast portion of the body.

Calcinosis cutis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calciphylaxis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calciphylaxis.question: The _____ was Painful, necrotic skin lesions associated with chronic kidney disease.
Calciphylaxis.fact: Calciphylaxis, also called calcific uremic arteriolopathy (CUA) or “Grey Scale”, is a rare syndrome characterized by painful skin lesions. The pathogenesis of calciphylaxis is unclear but believed to involve calcification of the small blood vessels located within the fatty tissue and deeper layers of the skin, blood clots, and eventual death of skin cells due to lack of blood flow.

Calciphylaxis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Calisthenics.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
